correctness.rationale: The exact inequality is B^n<A^(n+1) for A=pi(n^2)>0 and B=A+d=pi((n+1)^2). For n>=1000, Brun-Titchmarsh controls the number of new primes d<=2(2n+1)/log(2n+1), and Rosser-Schoenfeld pi(n^2)>n^2/(2log n). From log n<n/100 derive A>50n>=50000 and log A>9; meanwhile n log(1+d/A)<nd/A<8+4/n<9. The interval width satisfies required x>=1, y>=2 and y<=x in this range. Independently generated exact sieve to 1,000,000 (pi=78498) and arbitrary-precision powers check all 997 integers 3<=n<=999, matching inspected verify.py. All indices are covered; finite tests do not prove the analytic tail.

evidence: Brun-Titchmarsh and Rosser-Schoenfeld bound new primes/total primes separately; neither alone states B^n<A^(n+1). Conjecture 2.7(i) compares pi(kn) with pi((k+1)n) at fixed n, not consecutive squares.

originality.rationale: Sun Conjecture 2.14(ii) in the full 2014 prime-problems source is literally the same sequence pi(n^2)^(1/n); inspected the conjecture page. We did not locate a subsequent full proof after targeted Sun/prime-root searches and Resultary semantic comparison. Related Sun Conjecture 2.7 fixes scale n while varying multiplicative k and does not imply this next-square inequality by either natural substitution. Classical prime-counting estimates are prior; the claimed contribution is their use to settle this exact conjectured all-n monotonicity.
residual_risks: Unindexed or very recent proof of the same conjecture not excluded by search; prioritize continued historical verification before public originality certification.

value.rationale: This resolves a specific published prime-counting monotonicity conjecture for every n>=3, with a rigorously closed analytic tail and finite prefix. It is a natural boundary on growth of prime counts between consecutive squares and not an arbitrary small data check. It does not imply Legendre or Firoozbakht conjectures.

limitations: Root monotonicity applies to n>=3 and exactly the square argument; no other power family or prime-gap conjecture follows.
Independent finite closure n=3..999 is exact arithmetic; tail depends on published inequalities.
